faq.q: How does an AI model photo get made?
faq.a: It shows your garment on a virtual model. You start with a product photo of the canvas backpack and get a worn image for the store.

faq.q: Can I put my garment on a virtual model?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the garment photo, choose who wears it, and download the worn file. The guide to [model photos without a photoshoot](page:blog-model-photos-without-a-photoshoot) walks through that path.

faq.q: What kind of photo should I upload?
faq.a: Show the whole garment, with the color easy to read. A photo that cuts off the hem of the hoodie gives the model less shape to wear.

faq.q: How close is this to a studio photo?
faq.a: You pick the model, the pose, and the setting. Compare the worn photo with the upload before you publish. Fine seams can still shift.

faq.q: Which products can go on a virtual model?
faq.a: Clothing, bags, jewelry, and eyewear all work from a clear photo that shows the whole item.

faq.q: Can I reuse a model on the next collection?
faq.a: Yes. Save the model with your brand looks and start the next collection from that face.

faq.q: Can I create model photos for an entire collection?
faq.a: Yes. Run several garment photos in one batch, or send them from the shop software you already use. Each image is 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.
Use 9:16 for a story, 1:1 for a square gallery, or 4:3 and 16:9 when the page is wide. 3:4 is there for a taller product tile.

faq.q: Can I publish these photos on my store and in ads?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no watermark. Put the worn photo on the product page, and use a square crop in an ad. Keep a plain product photo beside it when shoppers need measurements.

faq.q: What if a small print looks different?
faq.a: Look at the worn photo next to the upload before you publish. Fine prints and seams can shift.
